scenario: A hospital administrator will assign exactly seven interns—Ogawa, Park, Quintero, Ramos, Singh, Tan, and Vance—to exactly three departments: Cardiology, Hematology, and Neurology. Each intern is assigned to exactly one department. Cardiology will have exactly three interns, Hematology will have exactly two interns, and Neurology will have exactly two interns. The following conditions apply: Ogawa is assigned to Cardiology. Park and Ramos are assigned to different departments. Quintero and Singh are assigned to the same department. If Tan is assigned to Neurology, then Vance is assigned to Cardiology. Ramos is not assigned to Hematology.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following could be a complete and accurate assignment of interns to departments?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Cardiology: Ogawa, Park, Ramos; Hematology: Quintero, Singh; Neurology: Tan, Vance

choices.label: B
choices.text: Cardiology: Ogawa, Park, Tan; Hematology: Quintero, Ramos; Neurology: Singh, Vance

choices.label: C
choices.text: Cardiology: Ogawa, Ramos, Vance; Hematology: Quintero, Singh; Neurology: Park, Tan

choices.label: D
choices.text: Cardiology: Ogawa, Quintero, Tan; Hematology: Park, Singh; Neurology: Ramos, Vance

choices.label: E
choices.text: Cardiology: Ogawa, Park, Vance; Hematology: Ramos, Tan; Neurology: Quintero, Singh

explanations.correct: This assignment honors every rule: Ogawa is in Cardiology; Park (Neurology) and Ramos (Cardiology) are in different departments; Quintero and Singh are both in Hematology; Ramos is not in Hematology; group sizes are 3/2/2.
explanations.A: Park and Ramos are both in Cardiology, violating the different-department rule.
explanations.B: Ramos is assigned to Hematology, violating the rule that Ramos is not assigned to Hematology. Also Quintero and Singh are in different departments.
explanations.D: Quintero (Cardiology) and Singh (Hematology) are in different departments, violating the same-department rule.
explanations.E: Tan is in Hematology—permitted by the conditional rule—but Ramos is in Hematology, violating the rule that Ramos is not assigned to Hematology.

questions.questionStem: If Quintero is assigned to Neurology, then which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Park is assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Ramos is assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tan is assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vance is assigned to Hematology.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Park is assigned to Neurology.

explanations.correct: If Quintero is in Neurology, Singh is too, filling Neurology (2). Cardiology (3) and Hematology (2) must be drawn from Ogawa, Park, Ramos, Tan, Vance. Since Ramos cannot be in Hematology and is not in Neurology, Ramos must be in Cardiology.
explanations.A: Park could be in Hematology; Park is not forced into Cardiology (for example, Ogawa, Ramos, Tan in Cardiology and Park, Vance in Hematology is permitted).
explanations.E: Neurology is already filled by Quintero and Singh, so Park cannot be in Neurology.

questions.questionStem: If Ramos is assigned to Cardiology, then which one of the following could be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Park is assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Quintero is assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Singh is assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vance is assigned to Hematology.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tan is assigned to Hematology.

explanations.correct: With Ogawa and Ramos in Cardiology, Park must be in Hematology or Neurology (different from Ramos). One valid arrangement is Cardiology: Ogawa, Ramos, Vance; Hematology: Park, Tan; Neurology: Quintero, Singh—so Tan could be in Hematology.
explanations.A: Park and Ramos must be in different departments, so Park cannot join Ramos in Cardiology.
explanations.B: Quintero and Singh must be together; Cardiology already has Ogawa and Ramos, leaving only one Cardiology slot, so the Q–S pair cannot fit in Cardiology.
explanations.C: Same reasoning as (B): only one Cardiology slot remains for the Q–S pair.
explanations.D: If Vance is in Hematology, Cardiology's third slot must go to Park or Tan. Park cannot (rule 2), so Tan is in Cardiology. Then Quintero and Singh fill Neurology. But Hematology needs two interns, leaving only Vance there—contradiction.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following CANNOT be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Quintero and Singh are both assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Park and Tan are both assigned to Hematology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Tan and Vance are both assigned to Neurology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Ramos and Vance are both assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Park and Vance are both assigned to Neurology.

explanations.correct: If Tan is in Neurology, the conditional rule forces Vance into Cardiology. So Tan and Vance cannot both be in Neurology.
explanations.A: Possible, e.g., Cardiology: Ogawa, Quintero, Singh; Hematology: Park, Vance; Neurology: Ramos, Tan—wait, Ramos cannot be in Hematology, and here Ramos is in Neurology, which is allowed. However Park and Ramos must differ: Park is Hematology, Ramos is Neurology—fine. But this makes Tan in Neurology which forces Vance into Cardiology, contradicting Q/S there. Let's try Cardiology: Ogawa, Quintero, Singh; Hematology: Park, Tan; Neurology: Ramos, Vance. Park≠Ramos ✓, Ramos not Hematology ✓, Tan in Hematology so conditional not triggered ✓. Valid.
explanations.B: Possible: Cardiology: Ogawa, Ramos, Vance; Hematology: Park, Tan; Neurology: Quintero, Singh.
explanations.D: Possible: Cardiology: Ogawa, Ramos, Vance; Hematology: Park, Tan; Neurology: Quintero, Singh.
explanations.E: Possible: Cardiology: Ogawa, Ramos, Tan; Hematology: Quintero, Singh; Neurology: Park, Vance. Tan in Cardiology so conditional not triggered.

questions.questionStem: Which one of the following must be true?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Ogawa and Ramos are assigned to the same department.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Quintero is assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Ramos is assigned to either Cardiology or Neurology.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Vance is assigned to Cardiology.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Tan and Park are assigned to the same department.

explanations.correct: Ramos is explicitly barred from Hematology, so Ramos must be assigned to Cardiology or Neurology.
explanations.A: Ramos could be in Neurology while Ogawa is in Cardiology.
explanations.B: Quintero (with Singh) could fill Hematology or Neurology instead.
explanations.D: Vance could be in Neurology (for example when Tan is in Cardiology).
explanations.E: Tan and Park need not share a department—e.g., Tan in Cardiology and Park in Neurology.
